test.prompt:
Add real-time search with debounce functionality to the following React component. The search should filter the displayed list as the user types, with a 300ms debounce to avoid excessive re-renders. Existing component: ```jsx import React, { useState } from 'react'; const ITEMS = [ { id: 1, name: 'JavaScript Framework Guide', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 2, name: 'Python Data Science Handbook', category: 'data' }, { id: 3, name: 'React Performance Optimization', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 4, name: 'Node.js Backend Architecture', category: 'backend' }, { id: 5, name: 'SQL Query Optimization Techniques', category: 'database' }, { id: 6, name: 'TypeScript Advanced Patterns', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 7, name: 'Docker Container Security', category: 'devops' }, { id: 8, name: 'GraphQL API Design', category: 'backend' }, { id: 9, name: 'CSS Grid Layout Mastery', category: 'frontend' }, { id: 10, name: 'Machine Learning with Python', category: 'data' }, ]; function ResourceList() { return (

Resources

    {ITEMS.map(item => (
  • {item.name} ({item.category})
    • ))}
); } export default ResourceList; ``` Requirements: 1. Add a search input field at the top of the component. 2. Implement debounce with a 300ms delay — do NOT use lodash, implement debounce yourself (custom hook or inline). 3. Filter items by case-insensitive substring match on the `name` field. 4. Show a "Searching..." indicator during the debounce delay. 5. When search input is empty, show all items. 6. Highlight the matching portion of text in each result (wrap matches in tags). 7. Show a "No results found" message when nothing matches. 8. Clean up the debounce timeout on unmount to prevent memory leaks. 9. Handle edge cases: whitespace-only input should be treated as empty, special characters in the query should not cause regex errors. Provide the complete, updated component code.

evalDetails.reasoning: Strong implementation covering nearly all requirements: custom useDebouncedValue hook with 300ms default and proper cleanup via useEffect return, controlled input filtering in real time, case-insensitive substring match via toLowerCase().includes, useMemo for filtered results keyed on debounced query, isSearching indicator gated to avoid flicker with 'No results found', highlightMatches using indexOf (not regex) to avoid special-character crashes, and .trim() handling for whitespace-only input on both live and debounced values. Cleanup on unmount is correctly handled by the useEffect cleanup closure. Minor deductions: the debounce is implemented as a debounced *value* rather than a debounced *callback/function*, which is a valid and common pattern but a purist might argue the 'debounce function' itself (as opposed to derived state) isn't explicitly memoized/useCallback'd — though this is a reasonable and arguably cleaner approach. The isSearching flag could theoretically be always true on first render equality edge cases, but trimming logic seems sound. The self-critique about toLowerCase() length changes for exotic Unicode characters (e.g. 'İ') is an honest caveat but represents an extremely minor, disclosed edge-case limitation rather than a bug. Code is syntactically valid, well-structured, uses idiomatic React patterns (hooks, memoization, controlled input), and includes accessibility touches (aria-live, aria-label) beyond what was asked. No crash-inducing special-character issue since regex was avoided entirely per requirement 9.

The implementation is thorough and hits every requirement: a real custom setTimeout/clearTimeout debounce hook (useDebouncedValue) with proper unmount cleanup, controlled input driving real-time filtering, case-insensitive substring match, useMemo-memoized filtering, a 'Searching...' indicator, whitespace-trimming, and a robust escapeRegExp (plus a defensive try/catch) preventing regex crashes on special characters. Two real but minor flaws: (1) the 'Searching...' indicator fires for 300ms on initial mount even though the user hasn't typed anything, since the debounce effect runs on mount too; (2) HighlightedText reuses a single global-flag RegExp object across multiple .test() calls in a .map loop, which is a classic JS anti-pattern (stateful lastIndex carried between calls) — on careful trace-through it happens to self-correct in all cases for this specific capture-group split structure, so it doesn't actually produce wrong output, but it's fragile, non-obvious, and harder to justify than the standard 'use split() index parity' approach. No requirement is unmet and nothing crashes; deductions are for code-quality/fragility and the minor mount-flash UX bug rather than functional failures.

The component correctly implements a custom debounce via a useDebouncedValue hook using setTimeout/clearTimeout (properly cleaning up on both value change and unmount), uses controlled input with useState, filters case-insensitively via toLocaleLowerCase().includes(), uses useMemo for filteredItems to avoid unnecessary recomputation, shows a 'Searching...' indicator while isSearching, trims whitespace so whitespace-only input equals empty, avoids regex entirely for both filtering and highlighting (so special characters like '.', '*', '(' cannot cause regex errors), highlights matches with <mark> tags via manual string index scanning (correctly handling multiple/overlapping-free matches), and shows 'No results found' when filteredItems is empty. Minor deductions: the debounce hook's isSearching flag is derived by comparing normalizedInput to debouncedQuery rather than an explicit loading state, which is a reasonable but slightly indirect pattern; also the highlightMatches function is not memoized (only filteredItems is), though this is a minor inefficiency since it only runs on render of filtered items. Overall this is a thorough, correct, well-structured implementation meeting all 9 requirements with proper React patterns and valid JSX.

Solid, well-structured implementation covering nearly all requirements. Custom debounce hook correctly implements 300ms delay with setTimeout, cleans up on unmount, and shows a 'Searching...' indicator. Filtering is case-insensitive substring match, empty/whitespace input shows all items, and special characters are handled safely via escapeRegExp for highlighting (filter itself uses .includes, not regex, so no crash risk there). No results message is present. Highlighting via HighlightMatch component works correctly using split on escaped regex. useMemo is used for filteredItems; useCallback wraps the change handler though it provides negligible benefit here since it's not passed to a memoized child. Minor issues: the isPending 'Searching...' logic has a subtle bug — since debouncedValue updates in the same effect that also sets isPending false only after the timer fires, isPending is set on every render where value !== debouncedValue including the initial pending render, which is roughly correct behavior but not memoized/debounced separately from the value-setting logic, coupling concerns in a way that's slightly non-idiomatic. Also isSearching won't correctly reset to false if delay changes mid-typing (edge case, low impact). The two normalizations (lowerQuery in filter, and query.toLowerCase() in HighlightMatch) are consistent. Overall clean, idiomatic React, syntactically valid JSX, thorough edge-case handling and a helpful requirement-mapping table.
